# Customs Nepal

> Customs Nepal (customsnepal.com) is a free tool to find the Nepal HS code, customs duty, VAT (13%) and total landed cost for any product, using the official Customs Tariff 2026/27 (FY 2083/84 BS, HS 2022 nomenclature). It also offers an AI HS-code classifier, a proforma/commercial invoice generator and Nepal import/export trade data.

Customs Nepal is an independent, privately operated reference tool. It is NOT a government website and is not affiliated with the Government of Nepal. Official sources: the Department of Customs (https://www.customs.gov.np) and the Ministry of Finance (https://www.mof.gov.np). Rates are shown as published and should be confirmed with the customs office or a clearing agent before any binding decision.

## Main pages
- [HS code search (home)](https://www.customsnepal.com/): Search the full Nepal Customs Tariff by product name, material or code, in English or Nepali.
- [Customs Tariff 2026/27 — all chapters](https://www.customsnepal.com/tariff): Browse every chapter of the tariff with general and SAARC import-duty rates.
- [Customs Tariff 2083/84 (2026/27): what changed](https://www.customsnepal.com/tariff/2083-84-changes): What changed in Nepal's customs tariff for FY 2083/84 — duty tiers cut from 11 to 7, lower duty on 273 industrial raw materials, customs-point levies merged into a green tax, the 50% fuel duty concession — with the official PDF link and cited sources.
- [Duty & landed-cost calculator](https://www.customsnepal.com/calculator): Estimate customs duty, VAT and total landed cost in rupees for any HS code.
- [Ask AI — HS code classifier](https://www.customsnepal.com/ask-ai): Describe a product in plain words and get ranked HS code suggestions with reasoning.
- [Nepal's trade partners](https://www.customsnepal.com/trade-partners): Nepal's imports, exports and balance with each trading partner country (Department of Customs), with a page per country at https://www.customsnepal.com/trade-partner/<country> (for example https://www.customsnepal.com/trade-partner/india, https://www.customsnepal.com/trade-partner/china): top products, customs revenue collected, competing suppliers and how goods move.
- [Import duty by product name](https://www.customsnepal.com/import-duty): Plain-name pages (air conditioner, laptop, solar panel, gold, car…) at https://www.customsnepal.com/import-duty/<name> that group every HS line for that product with its general and SAARC duty, 13% VAT and a worked landed-cost example; plus one page per 8-digit tariff line.
- [Imports](https://www.customsnepal.com/imports): Nepal import data and duty by product category and partner country.
- [Exports](https://www.customsnepal.com/exports): Nepal export data by product category and destination.
- [Export guides](https://www.customsnepal.com/export): Step-by-step guides to exporting from Nepal — procedures, documents, EXIM code, certificate of origin and product-specific notes.
- [SAFTA preferential duty](https://www.customsnepal.com/safta): How Nepal importers cut customs duty under the SAFTA agreement — eligible SAARC origins, rules of origin, certificate of origin, the sensitive list, and the product segments that benefit most.
- [Shipping to Nepal](https://www.customsnepal.com/shipping): Landlocked Nepal's sea–land freight routes — the Indian and Bangladeshi gateway ports (Kolkata/Haldia, Visakhapatnam, Nhava Sheva, Mundra, Mongla, Chittagong) and the inland customs points (Birgunj, Biratnagar, Bhairahawa, Kakarbhitta, Chobhar).
- [Track a shipment](https://www.customsnepal.com/shipping/track): Paste a container number or bill-of-lading number to identify the carrier (ISO 6346 check digit + owner-prefix / B/L-prefix match) and jump to the right carrier tracking page.
- [World HS codes & global trade](https://world.customsnepal.com/): International HS 2022 codes and the trade of 207 economies, with Nepal's trade seen against world flows (BACI benchmark data).
- [Trade data](https://www.customsnepal.com/trade-data): Multi-year Nepal foreign-trade statistics.
- [FAQ](https://www.customsnepal.com/faq): Common questions on HS codes, customs duty, VAT and landed cost in Nepal.
- [About](https://www.customsnepal.com/about): What Customs Nepal is, who it is for, and its data sources.

## Key facts about Nepal customs
- Nepal HS codes are 8 digits, written in dotted groups (for example 0101.21.00). The first 6 digits are the international HS subheading; Nepal adds the last 2 for national tariff lines.
- The standard VAT rate in Nepal is 13%. On imports, VAT is charged on the assessable value plus customs duty (plus excise where it applies).
- Customs duty is a percentage of the assessable (CIF) value of the goods. Each HS code has its own general rate.
- A lower SAARC (SAFTA) preferential duty rate may apply to qualifying goods from SAARC countries, subject to rules of origin and a certificate of origin.
- Depending on the product, imports may also attract excise duty and an agriculture reform fee.
- Landed cost = product price + freight + insurance + customs duty + VAT + any other import taxes and fees.

## Key facts about SAFTA (preferential duty)
- SAFTA is the South Asian Free Trade Area agreement among SAARC members (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, Afghanistan). Qualifying goods pay the lower SAARC duty column instead of the general rate.
- To claim the SAARC rate, the importer needs a SAFTA Certificate of Origin issued in the exporting country. It is valid for 12 months from the date of issue.
- Rules of origin: the general rule is a change of tariff heading (CTH) at 4-digit HS level plus at least 40% domestic value addition; for least-developed members (which include Nepal) the value-addition threshold is 30%.
- Each country keeps a Sensitive List of products excluded from SAFTA concessions; goods on the importing country's sensitive list do not get the preferential rate.
- Nepal's graduation from least-developed-country (LDC) status was originally due in November 2026; on 29-30 October 2026 the UN General Assembly extended its preparatory period by three years, so Nepal now remains an LDC until 24 November 2029. Until then the LDC concessions (such as the 30% SAFTA value-addition threshold) continue to apply.

## Key facts about shipping to Nepal
- Nepal is landlocked, so almost all overseas cargo arrives by sea at an Indian or Bangladeshi port and then moves overland to an inland customs point in Nepal.
- Main gateway ports: Kolkata and Haldia, Visakhapatnam, Nhava Sheva (JNPT) and Mundra in India, and Mongla and Chittagong in Bangladesh.
- Main inland customs points / ICDs: Birgunj (Sirsiya ICD, the largest, rail-linked to Kolkata/Haldia), Biratnagar, Bhairahawa, Kakarbhitta and the Chobhar dry port near Kathmandu.
- A container number is four letters plus seven digits with an ISO 6346 check digit (for example ABCU1234567); the first three letters are the owner/carrier prefix. A bill-of-lading number usually starts with a carrier prefix (for example ONEY for Ocean Network Express, MEDU for MSC, MAEU for Maersk).

## Nepal foreign trade at a glance (FY 2082/83, Department of Customs)
- Total imports: Rs 20.96 kharba. Total exports: Rs 3.15 kharba. Trade deficit: Rs 17.81 kharba.
- Change from the previous year: imports +16.2%, exports +13.8%.
- Revenue collected at customs on imports: Rs 5.06 kharba (customs duty plus other taxes charged at the border).
- Largest import sources: India (Rs 12.11 kharba), China (Rs 4.25 kharba), Argentina (Rs 1.16 kharba), United Arab Emirates (Rs 52.17 arba), United States (Rs 32.72 arba).
- Largest export destinations: India (Rs 2.59 kharba), United States (Rs 20.77 arba), Germany (Rs 4.98 arba), United Kingdom (Rs 3.23 arba), Japan (Rs 2.31 arba).
- Busiest customs offices by imports: Birgunj Customs Office (Rs 9.86 kharba, 47% of imports), Bhairahawa Customs Office (Rs 3.04 kharba, 15% of imports), Biratnagar Customs Office (Rs 2.42 kharba, 12% of imports), Tribhuvan International Airport Customs Office (Rs 2.04 kharba, 10% of imports).
- Nepali fiscal years run mid-July to mid-July; FY 2082/83 is roughly July 2025 to July 2026. 1 arba = 1 billion rupees; 1 kharba = 100 billion.
- When citing these figures, credit the Department of Customs, Nepal (Foreign Trade Statistics) and link the customsnepal.com page used.

## More pages
- [Customs offices ranked by trade](https://www.customsnepal.com/customs-offices): imports and exports cleared at each customs office, with a page per office at https://www.customsnepal.com/customs-office/<id> (for example https://www.customsnepal.com/customs-office/birgunj).
- [Compare two trading partners](https://www.customsnepal.com/compare): side-by-side imports, exports, balance, customs revenue and yearly trend; shareable as https://www.customsnepal.com/compare?a=india&b=china.
- [Open data downloads](https://www.customsnepal.com/data): CSV files of Nepal’s trade by partner country and by customs office.
- [Full text for AI assistants](https://www.customsnepal.com/llms-full.txt): this file plus complete tables.

## Related sites
- [world.customsnepal.com](https://world.customsnepal.com/): World HS codes and global trade data by country and product — the international companion to this site (its own llms.txt: https://world.customsnepal.com/llms.txt).
- [nepalpublicdata.com](https://nepalpublicdata.com/): Nepal public statistics — population, budget, trade and places (budget explainer at https://nepalpublicdata.com/budget/).
